A MuData file containing spatial transcriptomics data and a

:::
::: {.arg-attrs role="cell"}
`file` [required]{.arg-required}

[Example]{.arg-key} `"input.h5mu"`

:::: {.arg-row role="row"}
::: {.arg-name role="cell"}
`--modality`
:::
::: {.arg-desc role="cell"}
The name of the modality to use from the MuData object.
This specifies which AnnData object contains the spatial data.
:::
::: {.arg-attrs role="cell"}
`string` [required]{.arg-required}

[Default]{.arg-key} `"rna"`
:::
::::
:::: {.arg-row role="row"}
::: {.arg-name role="cell"}
`--obsm_spatial_coordinates`
:::
::: {.arg-desc role="cell"}
The key in `.obsm` where spatial coordinates are stored.
Expected shape is (n_cells, 2) for 2D coordinates.
:::
::: {.arg-attrs role="cell"}
`string`

[Default]{.arg-key} `"spatial"`
:::
::::

### Parameters

::::: {.arg-table role="table"}
:::: {.arg-row .arg-head role="row"}
::: {.arg-name role="columnheader"}
Name

Description

Attributes
:::
::::
:::: {.arg-row role="row"}
::: {.arg-name role="cell"}
`--density_bandwidth`
:::
::: {.arg-desc role="cell"}
Bandwidth parameter for Gaussian kernel density estimation in spatial units
(typically microns). Larger values create smoother density estimates.
:::
::: {.arg-attrs role="cell"}
`double`

[Default]{.arg-key} `50.0`
:::
::::
:::: {.arg-row role="row"}
::: {.arg-name role="cell"}
`--calculate_ripley_l`
:::
::: {.arg-desc role="cell"}
Whether to calculate Ripley's L statistic.
Warning: This is an O(N^2) operation and can be very slow for large datasets (>5000 cells).
:::
::: {.arg-attrs role="cell"}
`boolean`

[Default]{.arg-key} `false`
:::
::::
:::: {.arg-row role="row"}
::: {.arg-name role="cell"}
`--n_subsample_ripley`
:::
::: {.arg-desc role="cell"}
Number of cells to subsample for Ripley's L calculation.
If -1, use all cells. Recommended to keep this below 5000 for performance.
:::
::: {.arg-attrs role="cell"}
`integer`

[Default]{.arg-key} `-1`
:::
::::
:::::

## Example commands

You can run the pipeline using `nextflow run`.

### View help

You can use `--help` as a parameter to get an overview of the possible parameters.

```bash
nextflow run openpipelines-bio/openpipeline_spatial \
  -r v0.7.0 -latest \
  -main-script target/nextflow/feature_annotation/xenium_spatial_statistics/main.nf \
  --help
```

### Run command

::: {.callout-note appearance="simple" title="Create a params.yaml"}
The command below reads this component's arguments from a `params.yaml` file. To create one:

- generate it with the form on [Viash Hub](https://www.viash-hub.com/packages/openpipeline_spatial/v0.7.0/components/feature_annotation/xenium_spatial_statistics);
- see examples of using params files in the [guides](/guides/index.qmd);
- run several samples in one go with a [`param_list`](/guides/process-many-samples.qmd).
:::

Run locally with:

```bash
nextflow run openpipelines-bio/openpipeline_spatial \
  -r v0.7.0 -latest \
  -profile docker \
  -main-script target/nextflow/feature_annotation/xenium_spatial_statistics/main.nf \
  -params-file params.yaml
```

::: {.callout-note appearance="simple" title="Other backends and platforms"}
Replace `-profile docker` with `-profile podman` or `-profile singularity` depending on the desired backend. To run on Seqera Platform or through Viash Hub, see the [guides](/guides/index.qmd).
:::
